Definition: from G5311; lofty (in place or character):--high(-er, -ly) (esteemed).
BiblicalUsage: hypsēlós is the word for high, lofty, exalted. In Matthew 4:8, the text says "the devil taketh him up into an exceeding high mountain." In Mark 9:2, the text says "and leadeth them up into an high mountain apart by themselves."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, hypsēlós is a reminder that glory is the weight of who God is, and it is the end of everything He does. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: The Temptation in the Wilderness; Paul's Missionary Journeys; Transfiguration
